correctness.rationale: Zhang's theorem gives monotonicity of the normalized norm ratio including both endpoints. For positive exponents the circle moments are real analytic even with repeated boundary zeros, because local factors have the form |theta-theta0|^(m r) and parameter derivatives are locally dominated. Equality at two exponents therefore forces constancy on all positive exponents; the derivative identity at r=2 gives equality in the Lei--Zhang homogeneous entropy theorem, whose equality cases are exactly the regular-polygon binomials. For simple roots, the source area identity plus Harnack and |B(z)|<=|z| gives the stated weighted Dirichlet defect; direct radial integration yields k/(2k+1), and the entropy decomposition and derivative identity give the displayed prefactor.

value.rationale: The lead theorem is sharp but leaves equality stated only as attainment. Classifying the equality set is a natural extremal question and shows that every non-regular unimodular zero configuration separates strictly at every pair of exponents, including repeated-root configurations. The additional Harnack--Dirichlet lower bound supplies a nonzero, computable defect on the simple-root stratum, turning qualitative monotonicity into a stability certificate that vanishes exactly at the extremizer.
